    Track 3 · With BrewSLM · Lesson 11

    Training config reference: the brewslm.yaml manifest

    After this reference you can read a brewslm.yaml manifest section by section, identify which knob controls which behaviour, and know which fields apply actually writes versus only carries.

    Level: intermediate Read time: ~13 min Type: Reference Verified: 13 Nov 2026

    Track 3's narrative lessons described what BrewSLM does. This reference describes how a project is configured at the schema level. The canonical artifact is brewslm.yaml, a project-as-code manifest the platform exports, validates, diffs and applies. It captures the project-level settings a run starts from; per-run hyperparameters are set on the Train form and stored on each run, not in this file.

    This is a verified-contract page: every row was checked against the public BrewSLM code as of the Updated date at the top. A field is listed as applied only if apply writes it to the project today; carried, not applied means it validates and round-trips through export, but apply never reads it. Each row names the file where you can check it yourself.

    Why you would edit this file

    Most of the time you change settings in the workspace. The manifest earns its keep in three cases: you want a project's settings under version control and code review; you want to rebuild or copy a project somewhere else (apply with no project id creates a new one); or you want to change several project-level settings at once and see the before/after first. In the workspace the file lives under Ship → Package → Options → Project manifest (Pipeline as Code), which can import, validate, diff and apply; Settings → Export the project manifest only downloads it.

    Manifest envelope

    api_version: brewslm/v1
kind: Project
metadata:
  name: my-project
  description: "..."
  labels: { team: "ml", env: "dev" }
spec:
  # ten sections, all optional; blueprint defaults to null, the rest to defaults

    Any other api_version or kind is rejected. The schema is strict-extra-forbid: unknown keys fail validation, so typos and stale fields are caught by validate / diff / apply instead of becoming silent no-ops. metadata.name and description are applied (they become the project's name and description); labels is carried, not applied, and export does not write it.

    One caution before the table: a valid field is not always an applied field. Strict about keys is not the same as applied.

    The contract at a glance

    SectionField(s)Applied today?What apply does / where in the UISource
    workflowall sixappliedWritten to the project. Validate rejects an unknown pipeline_stage or target_profile_id.manifest_apply_service.py
    blueprintthe contract fieldsapplied when presentSaved as a new blueprint revision and made active. Left out: the project's blueprint is kept (warning blueprint_drop_not_supported).manifest_apply_service.py
    version, sourcecarried, not appliedProvenance only.schemas/brewslm_manifest.py
    domainpack_id, profile_idappliedResolved to the registered pack / profile. The diff has no domain row; the change shows only in apply's result. Settings → Tools → Domain Packs / Domain Profiles.manifest_apply_service.py
    modelbase_modelappliedBecomes the project's base model. Not in the registry: a warning, not an error.manifest_apply_service.py
    cache_fingerprint, source_ref, registry_idcarried, not appliedExport writes only base_model.brewslm_manifest_service.py
    data_sourcesentries, matched by nameappliedNew name: dataset created with its versions. Existing name: type, description, record_count, file_path, metadata updated; versions not re-applied. Missing from the manifest: a warning, never a delete. Data → Sources.manifest_apply_service.py
    adaptersentries, matched by nameappliedA changed adapter is written as a new version row (versions are immutable). Missing: a warning. Train → More options → Adapter Studio.manifest_apply_service.py
    training_planconfigappliedStored as-is as the project's dataset adapter preset. Not validated against TrainingConfig.manifest_apply_service.py
    training_mode, plan_profile, preferred_runtime_idcarried, not appliedShown in the diff if changed, never written.manifest_apply_service.py
    eval_packpack_idappliedValidated against the registered packs; becomes the project's preferred pack.manifest_apply_service.py
    datasets, eval_types, extracarried, not appliedShown in the diff if changed, never written.manifest_apply_service.py
    exportwhole sectioncarried, not appliedNot read by apply and not compared by diff; export always writes it empty. Formats are picked per export on Ship → Package.brewslm_manifest_service.py
    deploymentwhole sectioncarried, not appliedExport copies the project's target profile here; apply reads only workflow.target_profile_id.brewslm_manifest_service.py

    Paths are under backend/app/: services/manifest_apply_service.py (validate and apply), services/brewslm_manifest_service.py (export and diff), schemas/brewslm_manifest.py (the schema and defaults).

    Section notes

    Only what the table does not already say.

    spec.workflow

    workflow:
  beginner_mode: true
  pipeline_stage: ingestion
  target_profile_id: vllm_server
  training_preferred_plan_profile: balanced   # safe | balanced | max_quality
  gate_policy: {}
  budget_settings: {}
    • training_preferred_plan_profile is the preset for the next launch, and the only plan-profile field apply reads: safe (conservative), balanced (default), max_quality (longer training, more aggressive knobs). The Autopilot Planner (Settings → Tools → Autopilot Planner) is where it is normally chosen.
    • target_profile_id is the export/deploy target shape: vllm_server (default), mobile_cpu, edge_gpu and others in the target registry.
    • beginner_mode is the Settings → Workspace → Start advanced sections collapsed switch (default true): power tools open on request, nothing is hidden. The Coach notices have their own switch, Show inline tips, which is not a manifest field.

    spec.blueprint

    What the + New Project dialog's "What problem do you want this model to solve?" answer becomes. If you fill it in, the Coach notices and the auto-suggested pass/fail rules use the structured intent.

    blueprint:
  domain_name: "Customer support"
  problem_statement: "Classify intent of inbound tickets"
  target_user_persona: "Tier-1 agents"
  task_family: instruction_sft
  input_modality: text
  expected_output_schema: { ... }
  expected_output_examples: [ ... ]
  safety_compliance_notes: []
  deployment_target_constraints: { ... }
  success_metrics:
    - { metric_id: macro_f1, label: "Intent macro F1", target: "min 0.90" }
  glossary:
    - { term: "P1", plain_language: "Highest-priority ticket", category: "ops" }
  confidence_score: 0.0
  unresolved_assumptions: []
  version: 3                        # carried, not applied
  source: manual                    # carried, not applied

    spec.domain and spec.model

    domain:
  pack_id: customer-support
  profile_id: ticket-intent
model:
  base_model: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct
  cache_fingerprint: "sha256:..."   # carried, not applied
  source_ref: "hf:..."              # carried, not applied
  registry_id: 42                   # carried; re-resolved from base_model

    A domain pack ships defaults (synth playbooks, eval prompts, blueprint hints) for a vertical; a profile narrows it. Changing base_model is a real change: your next run starts from a different base. In the workspace it is the Base model field at the top of the Train form.

    spec.data_sources and spec.adapters

    data_sources:
  - name: tickets-train
    type: jsonl
    description: "Q3 labeled tickets"
    record_count: 4812
    file_path: data/projects/3/sources/tickets-train.jsonl
    metadata: { schema_hash: "..." }
    versions:
      - { version: 1, record_count: 4812, file_path: "..." }
adapters:
  - name: ticket-extractor
    version: 1                      # used only when the adapter is first created
    status: active
    base_adapter_id: default-canonical
    task_profile: instruction_sft
    source_type: raw
    field_mapping: { input: question, output: answer }
    adapter_config: { ... }
    output_contract: { ... }

    Adapters are the transformation layer between raw rows and the training-ready shape; adapter_config and output_contract are free-form because the adapter class defines the contract. The preset a split uses is picked on Data → Split.

    spec.training_plan

    The name suggests this section drives the trainer. It does not: apply reads only config, and that is a dataset adapter preset (keys such as adapter_id, adapter_config, field_mapping, task_profile), not a hyperparameter set.

    training_plan:
  training_mode: sft                # default sft; carried, not applied
  plan_profile: balanced            # carried, not applied
  preferred_runtime_id: null        # default null; carried, not applied
  config: { ... }                   # applied: the project's dataset adapter preset
    • training_mode: a run's own mode is one of sft (default), domain_pretrain, dpo or orpo. The training script also understands distillation (offline KD against captured teacher log-probs; Lesson 4.3), and the recipe.kd.* presets set it with distillation_offline: true. But the experiment API accepts only the four values, so a run created with training_mode: distillation is rejected, and offline KD is not reachable through a normal run today. Live-teacher KD works: an sft run with distillation_enabled: true and a distillation_teacher_model. (A fix that lets the experiment API accept offline distillation is merged but not yet released.)
    • plan_profile: export fills it from the same project field as workflow.training_preferred_plan_profile, so the two always match in an exported file. Edit the workflow one.
    • preferred_runtime_id: the registered runtimes are builtin.simulate (tests) and builtin.external_celery (real training through a Celery worker). A run picks its runtime from its own training_runtime_id config key; auto falls back to the server's TRAINING_BACKEND setting.

    Where the actual hyperparameter values live

    Not in the manifest. Learning rate, batch size, epochs, LoRA r/alpha/dropout, target modules, scheduler, warmup and precision are resolved when you launch a run and stored on that run's config. Change them in Train → More options → Model and hyperparameters / LoRA and advanced training; the confirm dialog before Launch shows the resolved config.

    spec.eval_pack, spec.export, spec.deployment

    eval_pack:
  pack_id: null                     # no choice saved: the domain profile's rules apply; a pack id becomes the choice
  datasets: [gold_dev, gold_test]   # carried, not applied
  eval_types: [exact_match, f1, hallucination, safety]   # carried, not applied
  extra: {}
export:
  formats: []                       # carried, not applied
  quantization: null
  extra: {}
deployment:
  target_profile_id: vllm_server    # carried, not applied
  extra: {}

    The pack named by pack_id declares the gates: the pass/fail rules on Results → Verdict (Lesson 3.13). gold_dev / gold_test are the platform's names for the answer key's practice and final halves (Data → Labels). Export formats the platform knows are gguf, onnx, tensorrt, huggingface and docker; you pick them per export, not here.

    Worked round-trip: change the plan profile

    Goal: make max_quality the project's preset. The same four steps work in the UI (Ship → Package → Options → Project manifest: paste or drop the file, then Validate, Diff against project, Apply, with a Plan-only preview (do not write) checkbox) or from the CLI, a thin client over the API (backend/scripts/brewslm.py, run as brewslm):

    # 1. export           GET  /api/projects/{id}/manifest/export?format=yaml
brewslm manifest export --project 7 --out project.brewslm.yaml

# 2. edit one field in project.brewslm.yaml
#    spec.workflow.training_preferred_plan_profile: balanced  ->  max_quality

# 3a. validate        POST /api/manifest/validate
brewslm manifest validate project.brewslm.yaml
# 3b. diff            POST /api/projects/{id}/manifest/diff
brewslm manifest diff project.brewslm.yaml --project 7

# 4. apply            POST /api/projects/{id}/manifest/apply
brewslm manifest apply project.brewslm.yaml --project 7 --plan-only   # preview, no writes
brewslm manifest apply project.brewslm.yaml --project 7

    Validate returns ok, errors and warnings; each issue has a code (for example UNKNOWN_EVAL_PACK), field, message and actionable_fix. A file that is not a valid manifest at all (an unknown key, a wrong api_version) is a 400 manifest_invalid:… instead. The diff is a ManifestApplyPlan; the part to read is the action rows. Illustrative output, real field names:

    {
  "project_id": 7,
  "project_name": "my-project",
  "api_version": "brewslm/v1",
  "actions": [
    { "target": "project",  "operation": "noop", "name": "my-project" },
    { "target": "workflow", "operation": "update",
      "before": { "training_preferred_plan_profile": "balanced", ... },
      "after":  { "training_preferred_plan_profile": "max_quality", ... },
      "fields_changed": ["training_preferred_plan_profile"] },
    { "target": "blueprint", "operation": "noop" },
    { "target": "model", "operation": "noop" },
    { "target": "training_plan", "operation": "noop" },
    { "target": "eval_pack", "operation": "noop" },
    { "target": "deployment", "operation": "noop" }
  ],
  "warnings": [],
  "summary": { "update": 1, "noop": 6 }
}

    One update row, on the field you changed: safe to apply. Apply validates again, and if there are errors it writes nothing and returns plan_only: true. Otherwise it writes in one transaction and returns applied_actions; here a single project update with fields_changed: ["training_preferred_plan_profile"]. Export again and both workflow.training_preferred_plan_profile and training_plan.plan_profile read max_quality.

    Now the trap. Had you edited training_plan.plan_profile instead, the diff would show a training_plan update with fields_changed: ["plan_profile"], and apply would write nothing for it: its result has a project noop, and the next export puts balanced back. A row in the diff means "this differs", not "apply will write this". Check the table above before you rely on an edit.

    What apply does with all of this

    Apply runs validate, builds the diff plan, and, unless validation failed or you asked for plan_only, writes everything in one transaction. Without a project id it creates a new project. Apply is non-destructive: the schema allows a delete operation, but apply never emits it. Datasets and adapters missing from the manifest become warnings (data_source_not_in_manifest:<name>, adapter_not_in_manifest:<name>), and a blueprint left out of the file is kept.

    Key idea

    brewslm.yaml is versioned (api_version: brewslm/v1) and strict (unknown keys are errors), so when the contract changes the next validate tells you. Strict about keys is not the same as applied: about half the fields only round-trip. Edit the applied ones, read the diff's action rows, preview with plan-only, then apply.

    The next reference catalogues the audit-spine surfaces that watch what runs do: the RunEvent taxonomy and the Coach action catalogue behind the inline Coach notices.

    Key terms

    brewslm.yaml
    The project-as-code manifest. Versioned (brewslm/v1), strict-extra-forbid, validates / diffs / applies against project state.
    Manifest spec sections
    The ten sections of spec: workflow, blueprint, domain, model, data_sources, adapters, training_plan, eval_pack, export, deployment.
    Training plan profile
    Named hyperparameter preset — safe / balanced / max_quality. Apply reads it from workflow.training_preferred_plan_profile; training_plan.plan_profile is carried, not applied.
    Training mode
    A run's mode: sft (default), domain_pretrain, dpo or orpo; not distillation (the offline KD recipes set it, but the experiment API rejects it today; live-teacher KD is an sft run with distillation_enabled). The manifest's training_plan.training_mode is carried, not applied.
    Eval pack id
    Registered pack reference like evalpack.general.default; the pack declares the gates — the pass/fail rules shown on Results → Verdict (Lesson 3.13).
    ManifestApplyPlan
    The before/after action list produced by manifest diff / apply — create / update / noop actions (apply never deletes), every unknown key rejected.
